steps: Read .github/scripts/apt-install.sh: each apt phase is bounded by APT_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (240) + --kill-after=10, and recover_interrupted_dpkg is bounded by another 240 + 10.
Worst case with APT_ATTEMPTS=2: attempt 1 (<=250 s) + dpkg recovery (<=250 s) + attempt 2 (<=250 s), about 750 s.
Compare with check.yml step 'Install system packages' timeout-minutes: 10 (600 s).
bugs.expected: The script's worst-case runtime fits inside the step timeout, so the final 'apt-install: failed after 2 attempts' line always prints.
bugs.actual: When apt ignores SIGTERM or dpkg --configure -a hangs, GitHub kills the step at 600 s before the final line prints. The per-attempt timing lines are already in the log. The normal hang case (2 x 240 s plus a fast recovery, about 480 s) fits. A flagged this itself; the task text asks for the same bound on recovery and a 10-minute step.
bugs.evidence: c-round-4.md (C-R4-01); .github/scripts/apt-install.sh run_bounded_as_root and recover_interrupted_dpkg; a-round-4.md code review section
